te.title: Off spec with the rotor at design speed
te.sit: Over the last shift AI-111 has crept from 9 to about 13 wt% (solvent-free). SIC-105 shows 180 rpm, the S/F ratio is 0.35, the feed is at design and nothing else is in alarm. What is wrong?

te.title: Hazy raffinate and a falling extract flow
te.sit: The stripper reports TCE droplets in the raffinate. FI-115 has been falling for ten minutes and PDI-110 has risen. Nobody has touched the controls.

te.title: The recovery column says the extract is wet
te.sit: C-103 phones: "your extract carries a water layer, our column is upset." LI-109 reads a steady 50 % and LIC-109 is in AUTO. The raffinate looks normal on AI-111.

te.title: Off spec at any rotor speed
te.sit: AI-111 rose above 10 wt% in the last hour. The day shift raised the rotor speed to 200 rpm: a small improvement only. Flows and temperatures are at design.

te.title: The mass balance will not close
te.sit: The shift report shows FI-114 + FI-115 about 170 kg/h more than FI-101 + FI-103. PDI-110 and XI-110 are higher than last week and AI-111 is creeping up.

te.title: Off spec after a solvent-meter calibration
te.sit: Instruments recalibrated FT-103 yesterday. Today AI-111 is over 10 wt% although FFIC-103 holds its ratio of 0.35 exactly. The feed is at design.

te.title: The analyzer says fine, the stripper disagrees
te.sit: To save solvent, the night shift lowered the S/F ratio to 0.31 because AI-111 showed plenty of margin (about 7 wt%). The stripper now complains that its acetone load is higher than usual.

te.title: Column pressure creeping up
te.sit: PI-108 has crept from 1.0 to about 1.3 bar g over the last quarter of an hour and PIC-108 output is climbing. Feed and solvent flows are steady.

te.title: The rotor keeps getting harder to turn
te.sit: JI-105 was 0.5 kW last week; today it is climbing past 1 kW and the vibration alarm has come in. The process side looks normal.

te.title: Warm column after chiller maintenance
te.sit: The rotor was raised to 212 rpm last week to tighten the spec. Since the chiller maintenance this afternoon the raffinate has turned hazy and PDI-110 is in alarm.

te.title: Off spec since the turnaround
te.sit: Since the turnaround the raffinate has drifted to 11–12 wt%. The same feed, ratio, rotor speed and temperature gave 9 wt% before. FV-103 now runs more open than it used to.

te.title: Flooding after a rate increase
te.sit: Planning asked for 15 % more feed. The shift raised FIC-101 to 1150 kg/h and, to keep the spec, the rotor to 205 rpm. Twenty minutes later the raffinate is hazy and AI-113 is in alarm.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Off spec with the rotor at design speed (C-101 RDC)
meta.caseTitle: Off spec with the rotor at design speed
meta.sit: Over the last shift AI-111 has crept from 9 to about 13 wt% (solvent-free). SIC-105 shows 180 rpm, the S/F ratio is 0.35, the feed is at design and nothing else is in alarm. What is wrong?

0.1.unit: C-101 extracts acetone from 1000 kg/h of 45 wt% acetone in water with 350 kg/h of 1,1,2-trichloroethane (TCE). Raffinate (top) to the stripper C-102 at ≤ 10 wt% acetone solvent-free; extract (bottom) about 50 wt% acetone to the solvent recovery column C-103. Rotor M-101 at 180 rpm (SIC-105).

rows.what: AI-111 11.0 wt% at start, 14.3 wt% after 30 min (spec 10)
SIC-105 shows 180 rpm, FT-103 350 kg/h, feed 1000 kg/h — all at design
AI-111 HI alarm; no other alarm

0.4.ctx: Told the shift leader (raffinate off spec, investigating); asked the lab for a raffinate sample; warned the outside operator that I may send him to the C-101 platform.

1.1.p: The raffinate has drifted off spec over the shift while the rotor, the ratio and the feed all look normal on the board.

rows.info: AI-111 raffinate acetone (solvent-free): 11.0 wt% at the start, 13.9 wt% after 15 min, 14.3 wt% after 30 min; design 9.0 wt%, spec 10 wt%. FIC-101 1000 kg/h, FFIC-103 350 kg/h (ratio 0.35), SIC-105 180 rpm: all at design.

1.4.why: Not a safety problem yet: no alarm is standing except AI-111, nothing is near a trip. It is a product problem: AI-111 is 11.0 wt% now against a 10 wt% spec, so acetone is being lost to the stripper every hour. If it is a mechanical fault it may get worse. Urgent within the shift, not an emergency.
1.4.park: Not needed: no safety limit near; keep running and hold the rate.

1.6.p: Interfacial area: drop size and holdup set by the rotor decide how much acetone is extracted.

ppl.msg: Stand by for the C-101 platform

R.1.p: Acetone moves from the aqueous feed (continuous phase) into TCE drops (dispersed phase). The rotor sets the drop size: faster discs give smaller drops, more holdup and more interfacial area a = 6φ/d, so more acetone transfers; too fast and the column floods.

modes.sig: JI-105 low, PDI-110 low, AI-111 up, AI-112 down
Balance out < in, D-102 rising, AI-111 up
PDI-110 and AI-113 up, FI-115 down

2.1.u: Inside: feed T-101 → P-101 → E-101 → C-101 (bottom); solvent D-102 → P-102 → E-102 → C-101 (top); rotor M-101 with SIC-105; raffinate PV-108 and extract LV-109; analyzers AI-111/112/113. Outside: the recovery column that sends solvent back to D-102.

rows.chg: None reported on the board; set points unchanged

2.10.p: Do not flood C-101 (XI-110 below 90 %, AI-113 below 1.5 wt%). Stay under the SI-105 HI alarm (230 rpm) and the JI-105 HI alarm (1.6 kW). Keep D-102 above its low level. Do not cut the feed unless nothing else works.

2.11.final: Bring AI-111 to 10 wt% or below and hold it for 5 minutes, with XI-110 below 90 % flooding, no alarm standing, feed kept at 1000 kg/h. Then find and remove the cause.

rows.what: Stroboscope on the shaft below the coupling
rows.means: Discs turn at about half the motor speed

rows.val: Hot, squealing, smell of burnt rubber

3.8.n: Six causes listed in the hypothesis table: analyzer AI-111 reading high; more acetone in the feed; less solvent than FT-103 shows; warmer column; solvent distributor damaged; rotor discs turning slower than the tachometer shows (coupling slipping).

4.1.ideas: Most likely: coupling slipping. Then analyzer error (cheap to rule out), FT-103 error and feed change. Most dangerous: none of these is a safety threat; the rotor one can get worse.

rows.act: Coupling and stroboscope in the field

rows.why: Checks the analyzer and the feed
Does the rotor respond as a healthy one would?

5.1.p: Balance: in 1350 = out 1350 kg/h. Lab raffinate 13.95 wt% against AI-111 13.89 wt%: the analyzer is right. Lab feed 45.0 wt% acetone, same as design (45.0). Field: coupling hot and squealing, a smell of burnt rubber; stroboscope on the shaft 94 rpm while SI-105 reads 180 rpm. Speed step to 200 rpm (20 min): JI-105 0.38 → 0.44 kW, shaft 104 rpm, AI-111 14.3 → 13.6 wt%; on a healthy rotor the same step gives JI-105 0.52 → 0.67 kW and AI-111 9.0 → 8.4 wt%.

rows.when: Rejected: above SI-105 HI; once the coupling grips the 2.2 kW overload trips the rotor

5.7.n: After 30 min: AI-111 9.30 wt% (spec 10), XI-110 47 %, AI-113 0.81 wt%, JI-105 0.48 kW, solvent 450 kg/h; balance 1450 in, 1449 out; SIS in RUN, no alarm standing. Target met and holding. D-102 falls slowly with the extra solvent (50 → 46.5 % in 30 min): told the recovery column, and the repair must not wait long.

5.8.rule: When a tachometer says normal but power, vibration and holdup disagree, check the shaft in the field.

rows.m: Coupling check on the monthly rotor round

6.2.p: Yes. Slower discs give bigger drops and less holdup (PDI-110 0.130 kPa), so less interfacial area and less acetone moves into the TCE: AI-111 up, AI-112 down, the balance still closes. Power check: 0.12 kW at no load + 0.40 kW × (94/180)³ = 0.06 kW into the liquid, and the rest of the 0.38 kW is heat in the slipping coupling, which is why it is hot.

hz.dev: Rotor speed MORE after the repair
hz.cause: Coupling repaired with SIC-105 still at 210 rpm

6.3.fut: When the coupling is repaired the discs jump to the set speed. Left at 210 rpm and ratio 0.45 the column runs at XI-110 82 % and over-extracts (AI-111 4.9 wt%) with 450 kg/h of solvent. Before maintenance restarts M-101: SIC-105 back to 180 rpm and the ratio back to 0.35, which returns AI-111 9.0 wt% and XI-110 75 %. Left at 340 rpm instead, the overload would trip the rotor and AI-111 would reach 27 wt%.

6.4.p: A soft alarm on rotor power against speed (JI-105 below the cube-law curve at the SI-105 reading) would have shown it at once. A second speed pick-up on the shaft below the coupling would remove the guesswork. VI-105 rising with no speed change is a hint too.

6.5.again: Lesson: when an instrument says "normal" but its neighbours disagree, believe the group, and check in the field. Recommendation: add a JI-105/SI-105 deviation alarm (about 20 % below the design curve) and a coupling inspection to the monthly rotor round; record the stroboscope reading on the round sheet.
6.5.never: A soft alarm on rotor power against speed (JI-105 below the cube-law curve at the SI-105 reading) would have shown it at once. A second speed pick-up on the shaft below the coupling would remove the guesswork. VI-105 rising with no speed change is a hint too.

R.2.eq: N = n·H·a·K·Δc (transfer rate);  interfacial area a = 6·φ/d₃₂;  rotor power P = P₀ + k·(N_d/180)³

sym.m: Interfacial area per unit volume of the active zone
Sauter mean drop diameter, set by the disc speed
JI-105 rotor power; no-load 0.12 kW and 0.4 kW into the liquid at 180 rpm
Speed of the discs (not of the motor when the coupling slips)

R.5.chk:
1 SI-105 against JI-105: is the power right for the speed?
2 PDI-110 and XI-110: holdup and flooding
3 AI-111 against a lab sample; AI-112 extract strength
4 Mass balance FI-101 + FI-103 against FI-114 + FI-115, D-102 level
5 Field: coupling, vibration, stroboscope on the shaft

1.3.safn: PI-108 1.0 bar g, TI-106 25 °C, levels normal; every trip is far away
1.3.envn: No release; the raffinate goes to C-102 as usual
1.3.eqn: VI-105 2.1 mm/s, below the 4.5 mm/s alarm; the coupling is wearing
1.3.prodn: Raffinate 11.0 wt% and rising against the 10 wt% spec: off-spec product to C-102
1.3.ttl: No safety limit is approaching; the spec is lost within the shift

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable condition that stops the problem growing while you investigate (e.g. a higher solvent ratio, rate held).
1.5.tc: A consequence (safety, environment, equipment) will arrive before the diagnosis is finished unless you act now.

rows.where: SIC-105 faceplate and JI-105 / VI-105 (Rotor display)
rows.what: Speed, power and vibration against design

2.5.a: with the rotor speed and solvent ratio, no new equipment
2.5.r: raffinate back to the stripper on spec
2.5.t: cause in 15 min, spec in 30 min
2.5.sf: XI-110 < 90 %, AI-113 < 1.5 wt%, no alarm standing
2.5.c: coupling repair at the next planned stop
2.5.goal: Bring AI-111 to 10 wt% or below and hold it for 5 minutes, with XI-110 below 90 % flooding, no alarm standing, feed kept at 1000 kg/h. Then find and remove the cause.

2.6.when: Over the last shift, still rising
2.6.where: C-101 active zone; the feed, the solvent and the balance are normal
2.6.why: Off-spec raffinate to C-102 and acetone lost
2.6.how: A slow drift, with JI-105, PDI-110 and AI-112 all low

rows.is: Too much acetone left in the raffinate (AI-111 high)
rows.isnot: Too little solvent: FT-103 350 kg/h, balance closes
rows.kill: Not a solvent or feed flow problem

rows.is: The rotor and holdup readings: JI-105, PDI-110, VI-105 off design
rows.isnot: Temperatures, pressure, levels, flows all at design
rows.kill: Not a utility or a control loop

rows.is: A slow drift over the shift

3.2.n: Rotor power at 180 rpm should be 0.12 + 0.4 = 0.52 kW; JI-105 reads 0.38 kW. The liquid part is only 0.26 kW, which the cube law gives at about 155 rpm: the discs turn slower than the tachometer says. The balance closes, so the flows are right.

3.5.tree:
TOP: AI-111 above 10 wt% at design flows
 OR — AI-111 reads high (analyzer)
 OR — feed richer in acetone
 OR — less solvent than FT-103 shows
 OR — column warmer than design
 OR — less interfacial area: discs slower than shown (coupling) OR distributor damaged
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets; no AND gate: any one path alone gives the top event.

rows.how: Killed by the lab: 13.95 against AI-111 13.89 wt%

3.10.n: None — everyone agrees the flows are right and the rotor readings disagree with each other

3.11.n: Nothing found in Explore contradicts the statement; it names no cause and stays valid

rows.step: SIC-105 to 210 rpm and ratio 0.45; watch XI-110, AI-113, JI-105, D-102
Work order: coupling repair at the next stop of M-101
Before restart after the repair: SIC-105 180 rpm, ratio 0.35

5.4.moc: Temporary operating change logged in the shift book; no MOC needed for set points inside the operating window.

6.0.n: Every prediction (lab = analyzer, shaft slower than SI-105, weak response to the step, fix → AI-111 9.30 wt%) came true.

evidence.text: AI-111 reads 11.02 wt% against its design value 9.03 wt% (spec 10).
JI-105 reads 0.38 kW against its design value 0.52 kW at the same 180 rpm.
PDI-110 reads 0.130 kPa against its design value 0.264 kPa.
AI-112 reads 47.9 wt% against its design value 50.1 wt%.
VI-105 reads 2.1 mm/s against its design value 1.2 mm/s.
AI-111 11.02 → 14.35 wt%; JI-105 steady at 0.38 kW; SI-105 steady at 180 rpm; XI-110 41 → 43 %.
Raffinate 13.95 wt% acetone solvent-free (AI-111 13.89). Feed 45.0 wt% acetone in water.
Motor humming, tachometer 180 rpm, vibration 2.1 mm/s, coupling hot and squealing, a smell of burnt rubber. Stroboscope on the shaft below the coupling: 94 rpm.

hyp.ifthen: If aI-111 analyzer reads high, then we should see: AI-111 high
If more acetone in the feed, then we should see: AI-111 high
If less solvent than FT-103 shows, then we should see: AI-111 high, AI-112 down
If column warmer than design, then we should see: Small AI-111 change
If solvent distributor damaged, then we should see: AI-111 high, PDI-110 lower
If rotor coupling slipping, then we should see: All: AI-111 up, AI-112 down, JI-105 low, VI-105 high, PDI-110 low
hyp.key: All: AI-111 up, AI-112 down, JI-105 low, VI-105 high, PDI-110 low
hyp.result: Shaft 94 rpm vs 180; coupling hot; step +20 rpm → shaft +10

tests.title: Lab samples: raffinate and feed
tests.move: Field ▸ lab samples of the raffinate and the feed. Nothing is changed on the plant.
tests.kill: Lab equal to AI-111 → WH-1 killed; feed at 45 wt% → WH-2 killed.

res.obs: Raffinate 13.95 wt% acetone solvent-free (AI-111 13.89). Feed 45.0 wt% acetone in water.

tests.title: Field look and stroboscope at the C-101 platform
tests.move: Field ▸ C-101 platform: listen, look at the coupling, stroboscope on the shaft. Nothing is changed.
tests.kill: Shaft at the SI-105 speed → WH-6 killed; shaft slower → WH-6 supported, WH-5 unlikely.

res.obs: Motor humming, tachometer 180 rpm, vibration 2.1 mm/s, coupling hot and squealing, a smell of burnt rubber. Stroboscope on the shaft below the coupling: 94 rpm.

tests.title: Speed step SIC-105 180 → 200 rpm
tests.move: DCS ▸ SIC-105 set point 180 → 200 rpm at 5 min, hold 20 min.

WH-6.note: A slipping coupling passes only part of the step: JI-105 and PDI-110 move little

tests.kill: A full response (JI-105 up about a third, AI-111 down clearly) → WH-6 weakened.

res.obs: Shaft 94 → 104 rpm (+10) for +20 rpm on SIC-105; JI-105 0.44 kW where a healthy rotor draws 0.67 kW at 200 rpm; AI-111 13.61 wt% after 20 min: a weak response, as a slipping coupling predicts.
